leo: Quick note — edge sample app hit weird TS inference when consuming our JS SDK. Generics collapse to `any` only after esbuild ESM bundle. Has anyone debugged this flow?

nora: yep. Common culprits: positional overloads + d.ts that exposes middleware-augmented intersections.

leo: minimal example I made:
```ts
// api.ts (published)
export function open(apiKey: string): Client
export function open(opts: OpenOpts): Client
export function open(a: any) { /* impl */ }
export function makeClient<T = unknown>(o: ClientOptions<T>): Client<T> { /* ... */ }
```
When I call `makeClient({ apiKey: KEY })` in an edge function, `T` is inferred as `any`. Locally (CJS) it's fine.

sam: try these quick checks:
- ensure sample-app tsconfig uses `module: "ESNext"` and `moduleResolution: "bundler"`
- avoid exporting intersection types from middleware; use a private symbol for metadata
- check package.json `exports` and `types` subpath — edge consumers read the `import` path first

nora: another non-breaking trick: add a branded auth type so TS picks the correct overload. Example: `type ApiKey = string & { __apiKeyBrand?: never }` and keep runtime unchanged.

leo: branding seems promising. Is there a downsides?

sam: tiny ergonomics hit for custom typings only, runtime unaffected. Also consider `typesVersions` if you need different declarations for newer TS.

nora: Also, if middleware mutates opts with `__retry` fields, cast that to `unknown` internally instead of changing exported `OpenOpts`. Keeps public shape stable so inference doesn't widen.

leo: good call. I'll: 1) switch retry metadata to Symbol, 2) add branded auth type to d.ts, 3) bump sample-app tsconfig to ESNext+bundler, 4) add a `tsc --noEmit` job to ESM edge CI.

devx-bot: created ticket js-sdk#420 "Edge ESM: overload inference and middleware metadata" and queued a CI job. :robot_face:

sam: lastly, add a short test that imports the published package from a fresh project using only ESM imports and runs `tsc --noEmit`. That catches these sooner.

leo: will do, thanks everyone.
